          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Thin colored line:</strong> the Tukey whisker range.
            More extreme model results can remain visible as dots outside it.
          </li>
          <li>
            Tightly grouped dots indicate better model agreement. A wide
            spread indicates more uncertainty about the exact percentile.

      </section>

      <section class="reader-guide-section reader-guide-section-wide">
        <h3>What do odds ratios and hazard ratios mean?</h3>
        <p>
          These measures come from validation studies and describe relative
          differences associated with a polygenic score. They are converted
          in this report into percentage change around a fixed 0% center.
          Values to the left indicate a relative decrease; values to the right
          indicate a relative increase.
        </p>

        <div class="guide-ratio-examples">
          <div class="guide-ratio-example">
            <div class="guide-ratio-example-value">OR 1.20</div>
            <div class="guide-ratio-example-label">
              Approximately 20% higher <strong>odds</strong> per reported score
              unit. Odds are not the same as probability, especially for common
              outcomes.
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="guide-ratio-example">
            <div class="guide-ratio-example-value">HR 0.80</div>
            <div class="guide-ratio-example-label">
              Approximately 20% lower relative <strong>event rate over
              follow-up</strong>. It does not mean an 80% chance or a guaranteed
              delay.
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>

        <figure class="guide-figure" aria-label="Example relative effect distribution">
          <div class="guide-effect-axis-wrap">
            <div class="guide-effect-axis" aria-hidden="true">

              <span class="guide-effect-dot" style="--study-color: #5B8DC5; --dot-left: 48%; --dot-top: 21px;"></span>
              <span class="guide-effect-dot" style="--study-color: #C4778A; --dot-left: 54%; --dot-top: 10px;"></span>
              <span class="guide-effect-dot" style="--study-color: #C4778A; --dot-left: 61%; --dot-top: 20px;"></span>
              <span class="guide-effect-dot" style="--study-color: #5FA083; --dot-left: 69%; --dot-top: 12px;"></span>
              <span class="guide-effect-weighted"></span>
              <span class="guide-effect-median"></span>
            </div>
            <div class="guide-effect-labels" aria-hidden="true">
              <span>Relative decrease</span>
              <span>0% · no change</span>
              <span>Relative increase</span>
            </div>
          </div>
          <figcaption>
            In odds/hazard plots, each colored dot is an ancestry-matched
            performance estimate. Estimates from the same validation publication
            share a color, so repeated results from one study are easy to spot.
          </figcaption>
        </figure>

        <ul>
          <li>
            <strong>0% center line:</strong> no relative change from the
            reference level.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Colored dot:</strong> one source-specific performance
            estimate included in the card.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Slate line:</strong> the estimate when only one is
            available, or the median when several are available.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>White line:</strong> SNPster’s weighted mean when multiple
            estimates are available.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Blue band:</strong> the middle 50% of estimates.
            <strong>Thin colored line:</strong> the observed range.
          </li>
        </ul>

        <div class="reader-guide-callout">
          These individualized transformations assume that the source effect
          was reported per standard deviation of the polygenic score. They are
          relative comparisons—not absolute disease probabilities—and can be
          misleading when the original study used a different comparison unit.
        </div>
      </section>

      <section class="reader-guide-section">
        <h3>How should model agreement be used?</h3>
        <p>
          Agreement describes how closely the retained PGS models place you
          on the percentile scale. It does not describe whether the result is
          favorable or unfavorable.
        </p>
        <ul>
          <li>
            <strong>Very high or High:</strong> models produce closely grouped
            estimates.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Moderate:</strong> useful information remains, but the
            precise percentile is less stable.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Low or Very low:</strong> models disagree substantially;
            interpret the card cautiously.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Not assessable:</strong> only one eligible PGS model was
            retained, so cross-model agreement cannot be measured.
          </li>
        </ul>
      </section>

      <section class="reader-guide-section">
        <h3>What makes a result more or less trustworthy?</h3>
        <div class="reader-guide-evidence-grid">
          <div class="reader-guide-evidence-item">
            <strong>Validation performance</strong>
            <span>
              AUROC or concordance describes how well a model distinguished or
              ranked outcomes in an evaluation cohort. Higher is generally
              better, but it is not a personal probability.
            </span>
          </div>
          <div class="reader-guide-evidence-item">
            <strong>Variant match</strong>
            <span>
              The share of variants from the published score that were
              available after your genotyping, imputation, and quality control.
            </span>
          </div>
          <div class="reader-guide-evidence-item">
            <strong>Ancestry relevance</strong>
            <span>
              The report prioritizes performance evaluations compatible with
              your broad genetic ancestry, but no reference population is a
              perfect match for every individual.
            </span>
          </div>
          <div class="reader-guide-evidence-item">
            <strong>Number and consistency of models</strong>
            <span>
              Several independently developed models that agree are generally
              easier to interpret than one model or a widely dispersed group.
            </span>
          </div>
        </div>
      </section>

      <section class="reader-guide-section reader-guide-section-wide">
        <h3>Important limitations</h3>
        <p>
          Polygenic scores capture only part of inherited susceptibility.
          They do not include all rare variants, family history, age, sex,
          medications, lifestyle, environment, screening history, or existing
          disease. A high genetic percentile does not guarantee disease, and a
          low percentile does not provide immunity. Decisions about testing,
          prevention, or treatment should be based on established clinical
          guidance and discussed with a qualified healthcare professional.
        </p>
        <div class="reader-guide-footer">
          <strong>Hover for detail:</strong> In the interactive report, hovering
          over model dots and markers reveals the PGS identifier, evaluated
          outcome, percentile, or effect estimate used in that visualization.
        </div>
      </section>
    </div>
  </div>
</details>

def make_metric_box(label, value, caption=None, extra_html="", status=None):
    if value is None:
        return ""

    caption_html = f'<div class="metric-caption">{html.escape(caption)}</div>' if caption else ""

    status_html = ""
    if status is not None:
        status_label, status_class = status
        status_html = (
            f'<span class="metric-status-tag metric-status-{html.escape(status_class)}">'
            f'{html.escape(status_label)}</span>'
        )

    return f"""
    <div class="metric-box">
      <div class="metric-label">{html.escape(label)}</div>
      <div class="metric-value-row">
        <div class="metric-value">{html.escape(value)}</div>
        {status_html}
      </div>
      {caption_html}
      {extra_html}
    </div>
    """


def make_meta_row(key, value):
    if value is None or pd.isna(value) or str(value).strip() == "":
        return ""

    return f"""
    <div class="meta-row">
      <div class="meta-key">{html.escape(str(key))}</div>
      <div class="meta-value">{html.escape(str(value))}</div>
    </div>
    """


def publication_summary(row):
    if row is None:
        return None

    joined_pmid = normalize_pmid_value(
        row.get("pubmed_id_pmid", np.nan)
    )
    if joined_pmid:
        return f"PMID: {joined_pmid}"

    joined_doi = normalize_doi_value(
        row.get("digital_object_identifier_doi", np.nan)
    )
    if joined_doi:
        return f"DOI: {joined_doi}"

    return publication_reference_value(
        row.get("publication_pmid", np.nan),
        row.get("publication_doi", np.nan),
        row.get("development_publication_pmid", np.nan),
        row.get("development_publication_doi", np.nan),
    )



def performance_metric_label_value(row):
    """Return the validation discrimination metric shown for one selected PPM."""
    if row is None:
        return (None, np.nan)

    auroc = row.get("auroc", np.nan)
    if not pd.isna(auroc):
        return ("AUROC", float(auroc))

    concordance = row.get("concordance_statistic", np.nan)
    if not pd.isna(concordance):
        return ("Concordance statistic", float(concordance))

    return (None, np.nan)


def formatted_performance_metric(row):
    """Return e.g. 'AUROC 0.74' or 'C-index 0.71' for tables."""
    label, value = performance_metric_label_value(row)

    if label is None or pd.isna(value):
        return None

    compact_label = "C-index" if label == "Concordance statistic" else label
    return f"{compact_label} {float(value):.2f}"

def add_source_metadata(meta_rows, prefix, row):
    if row is None:
        return meta_rows

    metric_label, metric_value = performance_metric_label_value(row)

    meta_rows += make_meta_row(f"{prefix} PGS", row.get("pgs_id", np.nan))
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(
        f"{prefix} {metric_label}" if metric_label else f"{prefix} discrimination",
        fmt_float(metric_value, 2),
    )
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(f"{prefix} variants matched", fmt_variant_match_summary(row))
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(f"{prefix} variant match %", fmt_variant_match_pct(row.get("percent_variants_matched", np.nan)))
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(f"{prefix} n variants matched", fmt_int(row.get("n_variants_matched", np.nan)))
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(f"{prefix} eval. N", fmt_int(row.get("evaluation_n", np.nan)))
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(f"{prefix} evaluation ancestry", row.get("broad_ancestry_category", np.nan))
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(f"{prefix} PSS", row.get("pss_id", np.nan))
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(f"{prefix} PPM", row.get("ppm_id", np.nan))
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(f"{prefix} literature", publication_summary(row))
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(
        f"{prefix} DOI",
        normalize_doi_value(row.get("publication_doi", np.nan)),
    )
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(
        f"{prefix} PMID",
        normalize_pmid_value(row.get("publication_pmid", np.nan)),
    )
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(
        f"{prefix} development DOI",
        normalize_doi_value(
            row.get("development_publication_doi", np.nan)
        ),
    )
    meta_rows += make_meta_row(
        f"{prefix} development PMID",
        normalize_pmid_value(
            row.get("development_publication_pmid", np.nan)
        ),
    )
    return meta_rows


def model_table_value(value):
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return ""
    return html.escape(str(value))



def split_cohort_names(value):
    """Split one database cohort field into distinct named cohorts."""
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return []

    raw = str(value).strip()
    if not raw:
        return []

    # "|" is used inside source cohort fields. " / " is introduced by
    # the SQL STRING_AGG when multiple cohort values belong to one PSS.
    parts = re.split(
        r"\s*(?:\||\s+/\s+|;|\r?\n)\s*",
        raw,
    )

    unique_names = []
    seen = set()

    for part in parts:
        name = part.strip()
        if not name:
            continue

        key = name.casefold()
        if key in seen:
            continue

        seen.add(key)
        unique_names.append(name)

    return unique_names


def cohort_display_value(row):
    """Display each reported evaluation_sample_sets.cohort separately."""
    if row is None:
        return "Not reported"

    cohort_names = split_cohort_names(
        row.get("cohort", np.nan)
    )

    if not cohort_names:
        return "Not reported"

    return " / ".join(cohort_names)


def count_unique_cohorts(df):
    """Count all distinct cohorts, including pipe-delimited source values."""
    if df is None or df.empty or "cohort" not in df.columns:
        return 0

    unique_cohorts = set()

    for value in df["cohort"].dropna():
        for cohort_name in split_cohort_names(value):
            unique_cohorts.add(cohort_name.casefold())

    return len(unique_cohorts)



def make_model_rows(models_df):
    """PGS-level summary rows: exactly one row per retained PGS."""
    rows = []

    for _, row in models_df.iterrows():
        rows.append(f"""
        <tr>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('pgs_id', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(fmt_percentile(row.get('percentile_norm2', np.nan)))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(formatted_pgs_summary_metric(row))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('n_ppm_evaluations', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('n_pss_evaluations', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(fmt_variant_match_pct(row.get('percent_variants_matched', np.nan)))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(fmt_int(row.get('n_variants_matched', np.nan)))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('broad_ancestry_category', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(fmt_int(row.get('evaluation_n', np.nan)))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('family_id', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('family_size', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('pgs_development_method', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(publication_reference_value(
              row.get('development_publication_pmid', np.nan),
              row.get('development_publication_doi', np.nan),
          ))}</td>
        </tr>
        """)

    return "\n".join(rows)


R2_METRIC_SPECS = [
    ("other_r2_value", "R²", "variance explained"),
    ("other_incremental_r2_value", "Incremental R²", "added variance explained"),
    ("other_partial_r2_value", "Partial R²", "partial variance explained"),
    ("other_adjusted_r2_value", "Adjusted R²", "adjusted variance explained"),
    ("other_liability_r2_value", "Liability R²", "liability-scale variance"),
    ("other_pseudo_r2_value", "Pseudo-R²", "model-fit statistic"),
]


def ratio_allowed(row, ratio_type):
    flag_col = (
        "odds_ratio_personalizable"
        if ratio_type == "OR"
        else "hazard_ratio_personalizable"
    )
    return bool(row.get(flag_col, False))


def format_r2_summary(row):
    values = []

    for column, label, _ in R2_METRIC_SPECS:
        value = row.get(column, np.nan)
        if value is None or pd.isna(value):
            continue

        numeric = float(value)
        if 0 <= numeric <= 1:
            display = f"{numeric * 100:.2f}%"
        else:
            display = f"{numeric:.3g}"

        values.append(f"{label} {display}")

    return " · ".join(values) if values else None


def make_metric_chip(label, value, note=None):
    if value is None:
        return ""

    note_html = (
        f'<div class="outcome-metric-chip-note">{html.escape(note)}</div>'
        if note
        else ""
    )

    return f"""
    <div class="outcome-metric-chip">
      <div class="outcome-metric-chip-label">{html.escape(label)}</div>
      <div class="outcome-metric-chip-value">{html.escape(value)}</div>
      {note_html}
    </div>
    """


def summarize_metric_values(df, column, digits=2, as_percent=False):
    if df is None or df.empty or column not in df.columns:
        return None

    values = pd.to_numeric(df[column], errors="coerce").dropna()
    if values.empty:
        return None

    if as_percent:
        values = values * 100.0
        formatter = lambda value: f"{value:.2f}%"
    else:
        formatter = lambda value: f"{value:.{digits}f}"

    median = float(values.median())

    if len(values) == 1:
        return formatter(median)

    low = float(values.min())
    high = float(values.max())

    if abs(high - low) < 1e-12:
        return f"{formatter(median)} · {len(values)} estimates"

    return (
        f"{formatter(median)} median · "
        f"{formatter(low)}–{formatter(high)} range"
    )


def make_outcome_metric_chips(outcome_df):
    """Non-R² validation summaries shown compactly beneath an outcome plot."""
    chips = []

    auroc_summary = summarize_metric_values(
        outcome_df,
        "auroc",
        digits=2,
    )

    if auroc_summary:
        chips.append(
            make_metric_chip(
                "AUROC",
                auroc_summary,
                "Discrimination for this evaluated outcome",
            )
        )

    cindex_summary = summarize_metric_values(
        outcome_df,
        "concordance_statistic",
        digits=2,
    )

    if cindex_summary:
        chips.append(
            make_metric_chip(
                "C-index",
                cindex_summary,
                "Concordance for this evaluated outcome",
            )
        )

    return "".join(chips)


R2_DISPLAY_SPECS = {
    "r2": (
        "R²",
        "Variance explained in the study-reported outcome",
    ),
    "incremental_r2": (
        "Incremental R²",
        "Additional variance explained after adding the PGS",
    ),
    "partial_r2": (
        "Partial R²",
        "Variance uniquely attributable to the PGS in the fitted model",
    ),
    "adjusted_r2": (
        "Adjusted R²",
        "R² adjusted for model complexity",
    ),
    "liability_r2": (
        "Liability R²",
        "Variance explained on the underlying liability scale",
    ),
    "pseudo_r2": (
        "Pseudo-R²",
        "Model-fit statistic; not interpreted as literal variance explained",
    ),
}


def r2_to_percentage_points(value):
    """
    Normalize R² values for display.

    Most catalog values are fractions (0.08 = 8%). A small number are
    already reported as percentage points (>1), so those are kept as-is.
    """
    value = float(value)

    if -1.0 <= value <= 1.0:
        return value * 100.0

    return value


def summarize_r2_values(values):
    values = pd.to_numeric(
        pd.Series(values),
        errors="coerce",
    ).dropna()

    if values.empty:
        return None

    pct_values = values.map(r2_to_percentage_points)

    median = float(pct_values.median())
    low = float(pct_values.min())
    high = float(pct_values.max())
    n = len(pct_values)

    if n == 1:
        return f"{median:.2f}%"

    if abs(high - low) < 1e-12:
        return f"{median:.2f}% · {n} estimates"

    return (
        f"{median:.2f}% median · "
        f"{low:.2f}–{high:.2f}% range · "
        f"{n} estimates"
    )


def make_r2_evidence(outcome_df):
    """
    Show all R²-family values linked to the PPMs in one evaluated outcome.

    Data come directly from data_libraries.pgs_performance_metric_values,
    so multiple R² entries within the same PPM are retained.
    """
    if (
        outcome_df is None
        or outcome_df.empty
        or r2_metric_data is None
        or r2_metric_data.empty
    ):
        return ""

    ppm_ids = {
        value
        for value in outcome_df["ppm_id"]
        .dropna()
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
        if value
    }

    if not ppm_ids:
        return ""

    subset = r2_metric_data[
        r2_metric_data["ppm_id"].isin(ppm_ids)
    ].copy()

    if subset.empty:
        return ""

    chips = []

    for metric_type, (label, note) in R2_DISPLAY_SPECS.items():
        metric_rows = subset[
            subset["metric_type"] == metric_type
        ]

        if metric_rows.empty:
            continue

        if metric_type == "r2" and "preferred_for_primary_quality" in metric_rows.columns:
            preferred = (
                metric_rows["preferred_for_primary_quality"]
                .astype(str)
                .str.strip()
                .str.casefold()
                .isin({"true", "1", "yes"})
            )
            metric_rows = metric_rows[preferred].copy()

        if "r2_scale_basis" in metric_rows.columns:
            metric_rows = metric_rows[
                metric_rows["r2_scale_basis"].fillna("").ne("ambiguous_scale")
            ].copy()

        display_values = pd.to_numeric(
            metric_rows.get("r2_estimate_display_percent", np.nan),
            errors="coerce",
        ).dropna()

        if display_values.empty:
            continue

        median = float(display_values.median())
        low = float(display_values.min())
        high = float(display_values.max())
        if len(display_values) == 1:
            summary = f"{median:.2f}%"
        elif abs(high - low) < 1e-12:
            summary = f"{median:.2f}% · {len(display_values)} estimates"
        else:
            summary = (
                f"{median:.2f}% median · {low:.2f}–{high:.2f}% range · "
                f"{len(display_values)} estimates"
            )

        chips.append(
            f"""
            <div class="r2-metric-chip">
              <div class="r2-metric-chip-label">
                {html.escape(label)}
              </div>
              <div class="r2-metric-chip-value">
                {html.escape(summary)}
              </div>
              <div class="r2-metric-chip-note">
                {html.escape(note)}
              </div>
            </div>
            """
        )

    if not chips:
        return ""

    return f"""
    <div class="r2-evidence-block">
      <div class="r2-evidence-heading">
        R² / explained-variation evidence
      </div>
      <div class="r2-evidence-grid">
        {''.join(chips)}
      </div>
    </div>
    """

def normalized_metric_rows_for_ppms(ppms_df):
    if (
        ppms_df is None
        or ppms_df.empty
        or performance_metric_data is None
        or performance_metric_data.empty
    ):
        return pd.DataFrame()

    ppm_ids = {
        value
        for value in ppms_df["ppm_id"]
        .dropna()
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
        if value
    }

    if not ppm_ids:
        return pd.DataFrame()

    rows = performance_metric_data[
        performance_metric_data["ppm_id"].isin(ppm_ids)
    ].copy()

    if rows.empty:
        return rows

    restricted = (
        rows["applicability_requires_match"]
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
        .str.casefold()
        .isin({"true", "1", "yes"})
    )
    comparator = (
        rows["metric_model_scope"]
        .fillna("")
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
        .eq("clinical_or_comparator_model")
    )

    return rows[~restricted & ~comparator].copy()


def _format_generic_metric_number(metric_type, value):
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return None

    value = float(value)

    if metric_type == "p_value":
        return f"{value:.2e}"

    if abs(value) >= 100:
        return f"{value:.1f}"

    if abs(value) >= 10:
        return f"{value:.2f}"

    if abs(value) >= 1:
        return f"{value:.3f}"

    return f"{value:.4f}"


def _single_generic_metric_summary(metric_type, row):
    estimate = _format_generic_metric_number(
        metric_type,
        row.get("estimate", np.nan),
    )

    if estimate is None:
        return None

    unit = safe_text(row.get("unit", np.nan))
    if unit:
        estimate = f"{estimate} {unit}"

    low = row.get("ci_lower", np.nan)
    high = row.get("ci_upper", np.nan)

    if (
        low is not None
        and high is not None
        and not pd.isna(low)
        and not pd.isna(high)
    ):
        low_text = _format_generic_metric_number(
            metric_type,
            low,
        )
        high_text = _format_generic_metric_number(
            metric_type,
            high,
        )
        estimate += f" · CI {low_text}–{high_text}"

    return estimate


def _multi_generic_metric_summary(metric_type, metric_rows):
    values = pd.to_numeric(
        metric_rows["estimate"],
        errors="coerce",
    ).dropna()

    if values.empty:
        return None

    if len(values) == 1:
        return _single_generic_metric_summary(
            metric_type,
            metric_rows.iloc[0],
        )

    median = float(values.median())
    low = float(values.min())
    high = float(values.max())

    return (
        f"{_format_generic_metric_number(metric_type, median)} median · "
        f"{_format_generic_metric_number(metric_type, low)}–"
        f"{_format_generic_metric_number(metric_type, high)} range · "
        f"{len(values)} estimates"
    )


def make_additional_quality_evidence(outcome_df):
    """
    Render normalized performance metrics that do not already have dedicated
    OR/HR/Beta/AUROC/C-index/R² visualizations.

    This prevents valid parsed metrics such as partial-r from disappearing.
    """
    metric_rows = normalized_metric_rows_for_ppms(
        outcome_df
    )

    if metric_rows.empty:
        return ""

    metric_rows = metric_rows[
        ~metric_rows["metric_type"].isin(
            GENERIC_METRIC_EXCLUSIONS
        )
    ].copy()

    if metric_rows.empty:
        return ""

    groups = {}

    for metric_type, type_rows in metric_rows.groupby(
        "metric_type",
        sort=True,
        dropna=False,
    ):
        metric_type = str(metric_type)

        label, note, group_label = OTHER_QUALITY_METRIC_SPECS.get(
            metric_type,
            (
                metric_type.replace("_", " ").title(),
                "Additional published performance metric",
                "Other published evidence",
            ),
        )

        if metric_type == "other":
            subgroups = type_rows.groupby(
                type_rows["metric_label_raw"]
                .fillna("Other metric")
                .astype(str),
                sort=True,
            )
        else:
            subgroups = [(label, type_rows)]

        for subgroup_label, subgroup_rows in subgroups:
            display_label = (
                str(subgroup_label)
                if metric_type == "other"
                else label
            )

            summary = _multi_generic_metric_summary(
                metric_type,
                subgroup_rows,
            )

            if not summary:
                continue

            groups.setdefault(
                group_label,
                [],
            ).append(
                f"""
                <div class="other-quality-chip">
                  <div class="other-quality-chip-label">
                    {html.escape(display_label)}
                  </div>
                  <div class="other-quality-chip-value">
                    {html.escape(summary)}
                  </div>
                  <div class="other-quality-chip-note">
                    {html.escape(note)}
                  </div>
                </div>
                """
            )

    if not groups:
        return ""

    group_order = [
        "Discrimination & prediction",
        "Correlation",
        "Classification & reclassification",
        "Other published evidence",
    ]

    group_html = []

    for group_label in group_order:
        chips = groups.get(group_label, [])
        if not chips:
            continue

        group_html.append(
            f"""
            <div class="other-quality-group">
              <div class="other-quality-group-label">
                {html.escape(group_label)}
              </div>
              <div class="other-quality-grid">
                {''.join(chips)}
              </div>
            </div>
            """
        )

    for group_label, chips in groups.items():
        if group_label in group_order or not chips:
            continue

        group_html.append(
            f"""
            <div class="other-quality-group">
              <div class="other-quality-group-label">
                {html.escape(group_label)}
              </div>
              <div class="other-quality-grid">
                {''.join(chips)}
              </div>
            </div>
            """
        )

    return f"""
    <div class="other-quality-evidence">
      <div class="other-quality-heading">
        Additional published performance metrics
      </div>
      {''.join(group_html)}
    </div>
    """


def format_other_metrics_for_ppm(ppm_id):
    if (
        ppm_id is None
        or pd.isna(ppm_id)
        or performance_metric_data is None
        or performance_metric_data.empty
    ):
        return None

    ppm_key = str(ppm_id).strip()

    rows = performance_metric_data[
        performance_metric_data["ppm_id"].eq(ppm_key)
        & ~performance_metric_data["metric_type"].isin(
            GENERIC_METRIC_EXCLUSIONS
        )
    ].copy()

    if rows.empty:
        return None

    pieces = []

    for _, row in rows.iterrows():
        metric_type = str(
            row.get("metric_type", "other")
        )

        label = OTHER_QUALITY_METRIC_SPECS.get(
            metric_type,
            (
                metric_type.replace("_", " ").title(),
                "",
                "",
            ),
        )[0]

        if metric_type == "other":
            raw_label = safe_text(
                row.get("metric_label_raw", np.nan)
            )
            if raw_label:
                label = raw_label

        summary = _single_generic_metric_summary(
            metric_type,
            row,
        )

        if summary:
            pieces.append(
                f"{label} {summary}"
            )

    unique_pieces = list(
        dict.fromkeys(pieces)
    )

    return (
        " · ".join(unique_pieces)
        if unique_pieces
        else None
    )


def beta_axis_labels(axis_limit):
    """Five symmetric beta labels with β=0 fixed at the center."""
    limit = float(axis_limit)

    ticks = [
        (0.0, -limit),
        (25.0, -limit / 2.0),
        (50.0, 0.0),
        (75.0, limit / 2.0),
        (100.0, limit),
    ]

    labels = []

    for index, (position, value) in enumerate(ticks):
        edge_class = ""

        if index == 0:
            edge_class = " edge-left"
        elif index == len(ticks) - 1:
            edge_class = " edge-right"

        label = (
            "0"
            if abs(float(value)) < 1e-12
            else f"{float(value):+.3g}"
        )

        labels.append(
            f'<span class="scale-axis-label{edge_class}" '
            f'style="left: {position:.1f}%;">{label}</span>'
        )

    return f"""
    <div class="scale-axis-labels"
         aria-label="Beta effect axis centered on zero">
      {''.join(labels)}
    </div>
    """


def _beta_unit_label(value):
    if value is None:
        return "study-reported units"

    try:
        if pd.isna(value):
            return "study-reported units"
    except TypeError:
        pass

    value = str(value).strip()
    return value or "study-reported units"


def _make_beta_unit_panel(
    beta_df,
    unit_label,
    local_color_map=None,
):
    values = beta_df[
        "individual_beta_shift"
    ].astype(float).to_numpy()

    n = len(values)
    median = float(np.median(values))
    q1 = float(np.percentile(values, 25))
    q3 = float(np.percentile(values, 75))
    low = float(np.min(values))
    high = float(np.max(values))

    axis_limit = nice_symmetric_axis_limit(
        max(abs(low), abs(high), .01) * 1.10,
        minimum=.01,
    )
    axis_low = -axis_limit
    axis_span = axis_limit * 2.0

    def position(value):
        return max(
            0.0,
            min(
                100.0,
                (
                    (float(value) - axis_low)
                    / axis_span
                )
                * 100.0,
            ),
        )

    jitter_offsets = [-5, 2, -2, 5, 0, -4, 4, 1]
    points = []

    for point_index, row in beta_df.reset_index(
        drop=True
    ).iterrows():
        shift = float(
            row["individual_beta_shift"]
        )
        beta = pd.to_numeric(
            row.get("beta_effect", np.nan),
            errors="coerce",
        )
        z_value = pd.to_numeric(
            row.get("z_norm2", np.nan),
            errors="coerce",
        )
        pgs_id = safe_text(
            row.get("pgs_id", np.nan)
        ) or "PGS"

        study_key, study_label = performance_study_identity(
            row
        )
        color = study_color_local(
            study_key,
            local_color_map,
        )
        jitter = jitter_offsets[
            point_index % len(jitter_offsets)
        ]

        beta_text = (
            f"β {beta:+.4g} {unit_label} per PGS SD"
            if not pd.isna(beta)
            else "β not available"
        )
        z_text = (
            f"z {z_value:+.3g}"
            if not pd.isna(z_value)
            else "z not available"
        )

        points.append(
            f'<span class="effect-distribution-point" '
            f'title="{html.escape(pgs_id)} · '
            f'{html.escape(study_label)} · '
            f'{html.escape(beta_text)} · '
            f'{html.escape(z_text)} · '
            f'personalized shift '
            f'{shift:+.4g} {html.escape(unit_label)}" '
            f'style="--study-color: {color}; '
            f'--jitter-y: {jitter}px; '
            f'left: {position(shift):.2f}%;"></span>'
        )

    range_html = ""
    if n >= 2 and high > low:
        range_html = (
            f'<div class="effect-distribution-range fill-beta" '
            f'style="left: {position(low):.2f}%; '
            f'width: {position(high) - position(low):.2f}%;"></div>'
        )

    iqr_html = ""
    if n >= 3 and q3 > q1:
        iqr_html = (
            f'<div class="effect-distribution-iqr fill-beta" '
            f'style="left: {position(q1):.2f}%; '
            f'width: {position(q3) - position(q1):.2f}%;"></div>'
        )

    n_studies = len({
        performance_study_identity(row)[0]
        for _, row in beta_df.iterrows()
    })

    caption = (
        f"Median personalized shift "
        f"{median:+.3g} {unit_label}"
        + (
            f" · IQR {q1:+.3g} to {q3:+.3g} "
            f"{unit_label}"
            if n >= 3
            else ""
        )
        + f" · {n} {plural_word(n, 'estimate')}"
        + f" · {n_studies} "
        f"{plural_word(n_studies, 'study', 'studies')}"
    )

    return f"""
    <div class="effect-bar-panel">
      <div class="effect-bar-topline">
        <div class="effect-bar-label">
          Beta-based shift · {html.escape(unit_label)}
        </div>
        <div class="effect-bar-value">
          {median:+.3g} {html.escape(unit_label)}
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="effect-distribution">
        <div class="effect-distribution-track multi-model">
          <div class="effect-distribution-axis"></div>
          {range_html}
          {iqr_html}
          <div class="effect-distribution-zero"
               title="No shift (0)"
               style="left: 50%;"></div>
          {''.join(points)}
          <div class="effect-distribution-median"
               title="Median personalized shift"
               style="left: {position(median):.2f}%;"></div>
        </div>

        {beta_axis_labels(axis_limit)}
      </div>

      <div class="effect-bar-caption">
        {html.escape(caption)}
      </div>
    </div>
    """


def make_beta_evidence(
    outcome_df,
    local_color_map=None,
):
    """
    Personalized beta shift = beta × z_norm2.

    If studies report incompatible beta units, they are kept as separate
    beta plots within the same evaluated-outcome section.
    """
    if (
        outcome_df is None
        or outcome_df.empty
        or "individual_beta_shift" not in outcome_df.columns
    ):
        return ""

    beta_df = outcome_df.copy()
    beta_df["individual_beta_shift"] = pd.to_numeric(
        beta_df["individual_beta_shift"],
        errors="coerce",
    )
    beta_df = beta_df[
        beta_df["individual_beta_shift"].notna()
    ].copy()

    if beta_df.empty:
        return ""

    if "beta_unit" not in beta_df.columns:
        beta_df["beta_unit"] = None

    beta_df["_beta_unit_display"] = beta_df[
        "beta_unit"
    ].apply(_beta_unit_label)

    panels = []

    for unit_label, unit_df in beta_df.groupby(
        "_beta_unit_display",
        sort=False,
        dropna=False,
    ):
        panels.append(
            _make_beta_unit_panel(
                unit_df,
                str(unit_label),
                local_color_map=local_color_map,
            )
        )

    return "".join(panels)


def make_published_group_comparisons(outcome_df):
    raw_columns = [
        "other_group_odds_ratio_raw",
        "other_group_hazard_ratio_raw",
        "other_relative_risk_raw",
        "other_relative_risk_ratio_raw",
        "other_incidence_rate_ratio_raw",
    ]

    entries = []
    seen = set()

    for column in raw_columns:
        if column not in outcome_df.columns:
            continue

        for value in outcome_df[column].dropna().astype(str):
            value = value.strip()
            if not value or value.casefold() in seen:
                continue

            seen.add(value.casefold())
            entries.append(value)

    if not entries:
        return ""

    items = "".join(
        f"<li>{html.escape(value)}</li>"
        for value in entries
    )

    return f"""
    <details class="published-contrast-details">
      <summary>
        Published risk-group comparisons · {len(entries)}
      </summary>
      <ul class="published-contrast-list">
        {items}
      </ul>
    </details>
    """


def _normalized_outcome_fallback(value):
    """Stable fallback grouping key when no curated outcome key exists."""
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return "other_evaluation_outcome"

    text_value = str(value).strip().casefold()
    text_value = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", text_value)
    return text_value.strip("_") or "other_evaluation_outcome"


def _outcome_group_key(row):
    """Prefer the curated database key; fall back to normalized clean text."""
    curated_key = row.get("evaluation_outcome_key", np.nan)

    if (
        curated_key is not None
        and not pd.isna(curated_key)
        and str(curated_key).strip()
    ):
        return str(curated_key).strip().casefold()

    cleaned = row.get(
        "evaluation_outcome_clean",
        row.get("specific_trait", np.nan),
    )
    return _normalized_outcome_fallback(cleaned)


def _outcome_group_label(outcome_df, group_key):
    """
    Pick one clean customer-facing label for an aggregated evaluated outcome.

    If the curated key corresponds to the target report trait, use the target
    trait label. Otherwise use the shortest cleaned label in the group, which
    tends to remove study-specific wording while preserving genuinely distinct
    outcomes.
    """
    target_values = (
        outcome_df.get(
            "evaluation_target_trait",
            pd.Series(dtype="object"),
        )
        .dropna()
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
    )

    for target in target_values:
        if (
            target
            and _normalized_outcome_fallback(target) == group_key
        ):
            return target

    cleaned_values = (
        outcome_df.get(
            "evaluation_outcome_clean",
            pd.Series(dtype="object"),
        )
        .dropna()
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
    )
    cleaned_values = cleaned_values[cleaned_values.ne("")]

    if cleaned_values.empty:
        return str(group_key).replace("_", " ").strip().capitalize()

    # First collapse casing-only duplicates.
    by_casefold = {}

    for value in cleaned_values:
        folded = value.casefold()
        current = by_casefold.get(folded)

        if current is None:
            by_casefold[folded] = value
            continue

        # Prefer conventional sentence/title casing over all-lowercase.
        current_score = (
            int(current[:1].isupper()),
            -len(current),
        )
        value_score = (
            int(value[:1].isupper()),
            -len(value),
        )

        if value_score > current_score:
            by_casefold[folded] = value

    candidates = list(by_casefold.values())

    # Prefer the concise canonical expression when several study descriptions
    # map to the same curated key.
    return min(
        candidates,
        key=lambda value: (
            len(value),
            value.casefold(),
        ),
    )


def _study_count(df):
    if df is None or df.empty:
        return 0

    return len({
        performance_study_identity(row)[0]
        for _, row in df.iterrows()
    })


def make_restricted_evidence_note(ppms_df):
    """Explain PPMs retained for transparency but excluded from general use."""
    if ppms_df is None or ppms_df.empty:
        return ""

    n_ppms = int(
        ppms_df["ppm_id"].dropna().astype(str).nunique()
    )
    reasons = []
    if "applicability_reason" in ppms_df.columns:
        reasons = [
            str(value).strip()
            for value in ppms_df["applicability_reason"].dropna().unique().tolist()
            if str(value).strip()
        ]

    reason_html = ""
    if reasons:
        shown = reasons[:4]
        reason_html = "<ul>" + "".join(
            f"<li>{html.escape(reason)}</li>" for reason in shown
        ) + "</ul>"
        if len(reasons) > len(shown):
            reason_html += (
                f"<div>+ {len(reasons) - len(shown)} additional restricted contexts.</div>"
            )

    return f"""
    <div class="reader-guide-callout">
      <strong>Restricted validation evidence not applied to this result.</strong>
      {n_ppms} {plural_word(n_ppms, "performance record")} required an explicit
      age, condition, sex, carrier, case-only, or other subgroup match. SNPster
      currently keeps these records for transparency but excludes them from
      personalized OR/HR/Beta transformations, primary AUROC/C-index quality,
      and the main outcome-evidence summaries unless user eligibility is known.
      {reason_html}
    </div>
    """


def make_outcome_evidence_sections(ppms_df):
    """
    Render one flat evidence row per UNIQUE curated evaluation outcome.

    All PPM estimates from every study/paper reporting that outcome are pooled
    into the same OR/HR/Beta distribution plot. Different evaluated outcomes
    remain separate.
    """
    if ppms_df is None or ppms_df.empty:
        return ""

    display_df = ppms_df.copy()

    # One validation-publication palette per consumer card. This keeps a
    # publication's color stable across all evaluated-outcome plots in that
    # card while still maximizing color separation locally.
    local_color_map = build_local_study_color_map(display_df)

    display_df["_outcome_group_key"] = display_df.apply(
        _outcome_group_key,
        axis=1,
    )

    grouped_outcomes = []

    for group_key, outcome_df in display_df.groupby(
        "_outcome_group_key",
        sort=False,
        dropna=False,
    ):
        label = _outcome_group_label(
            outcome_df,
            str(group_key),
        )

        grouped_outcomes.append(
            (
                label,
                str(group_key),
                outcome_df.copy(),
            )
        )

    # Put the most evidence-rich outcomes first, then alphabetically.
    grouped_outcomes.sort(
        key=lambda item: (
            -int(
                item[2]["ppm_id"]
                .dropna()
                .astype(str)
                .nunique()
            ),
            item[0].casefold(),
        )
    )

    groups = []

    for outcome_label, group_key, outcome_df in grouped_outcomes:
        odds_df = outcome_df[
            outcome_df["individual_odds_ratio"].notna()
        ].copy()

        hazard_df = outcome_df[
            outcome_df["individual_hazard_ratio"].notna()
        ].copy()

        odds_bar = make_effect_bar_panel(
            "Odds-based risk",
            odds_df,
            "individual_odds_ratio",
            "odds_ratio_effect",
            "OR",
            local_color_map=local_color_map,
        )

        hazard_bar = make_effect_bar_panel(
            "Hazard-based risk",
            hazard_df,
            "individual_hazard_ratio",
            "hazard_ratio_effect",
            "HR",
            local_color_map=local_color_map,
        )

        beta_html = make_beta_evidence(outcome_df, local_color_map=local_color_map)

        plot_items = "".join([
            odds_bar,
            hazard_bar,
            beta_html,
        ])

        plot_html = (
            f'<div class="effect-bar-stack">{plot_items}</div>'
            if plot_items.strip()
            else ""
        )

        chips_html = make_outcome_metric_chips(outcome_df)
        r2_html = make_r2_evidence(outcome_df)
        other_quality_html = make_additional_quality_evidence(
            outcome_df
        )
        contrasts_html = make_published_group_comparisons(
            outcome_df
        )

        if not any(
            value.strip()
            for value in [
                plot_html,
                chips_html,
                r2_html,
                other_quality_html,
                contrasts_html,
            ]
        ):
            continue

        n_ppms = int(
            outcome_df["ppm_id"]
            .dropna()
            .astype(str)
            .nunique()
        )

        n_studies = _study_count(outcome_df)

        groups.append(
            f"""
            <section class="outcome-evidence-group">
              <div class="outcome-evidence-group-header">
                <div class="outcome-evidence-group-title">
                  {html.escape(str(outcome_label))}
                </div>
                <div class="outcome-evidence-group-meta">
                  {n_ppms} {plural_word(n_ppms, "estimate")} ·
                  {n_studies} {plural_word(n_studies, "study", "studies")}
                </div>
              </div>

              {plot_html}

              {
                  f'<div class="outcome-metric-chips">{chips_html}</div>'
                  if chips_html
                  else ''
              }

              {r2_html}

              {other_quality_html}

              {contrasts_html}
            </section>
            """
        )

    if not groups:
        return ""

    return f"""
    <section class="outcome-evidence-section">
      <div class="outcome-evidence-heading">
        <div class="outcome-evidence-kicker">
          Outcome-specific validation evidence
        </div>
        <div class="outcome-evidence-title">
          Evidence across published studies
        </div>
        <div class="outcome-evidence-intro">
          Each row represents one unique evaluated outcome. Estimates from all
          papers evaluating the same outcome are shown together in the same
          distribution plot; point colors identify the publication. Different
          outcomes remain separate, and OR and HR are not mixed onto one scale.
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="outcome-evidence-list">
        {''.join(groups)}
      </div>
    </section>
    """


def make_ppm_rows(ppms_df):
    """Detailed routed performance rows with explicit metric semantics."""
    rows = []

    sort_cols = [
        col
        for col in [
            "evaluation_outcome_clean",
            "pgs_id",
            "pss_id",
            "ppm_id",
        ]
        if col in ppms_df.columns
    ]

    display_df = (
        ppms_df.sort_values(sort_cols)
        if sort_cols
        else ppms_df
    )

    for _, row in display_df.iterrows():
        odds = (
            effect_per_sd_text(
                row,
                "odds_ratio_effect",
                "OR",
            )
            if ratio_allowed(row, "OR")
            else None
        )
        hazard = (
            effect_per_sd_text(
                row,
                "hazard_ratio_effect",
                "HR",
            )
            if ratio_allowed(row, "HR")
            else None
        )

        beta_value = row.get("beta_effect", np.nan)
        beta_text = (
            f"β per SD {float(beta_value):+.3g}"
            if beta_value is not None and not pd.isna(beta_value)
            else None
        )

        discrimination_parts = []
        if row.get("auroc", np.nan) is not None and not pd.isna(
            row.get("auroc", np.nan)
        ):
            discrimination_parts.append(
                f"AUROC {float(row['auroc']):.2f}"
            )
        if (
            row.get("concordance_statistic", np.nan) is not None
            and not pd.isna(
                row.get("concordance_statistic", np.nan)
            )
        ):
            discrimination_parts.append(
                f"C-index {float(row['concordance_statistic']):.2f}"
            )

        r2_text = format_r2_summary(row)
        other_metrics_text = format_other_metrics_for_ppm(
            row.get("ppm_id", np.nan)
        )
        pub = publication_summary(row)

        outcome = row.get(
            "evaluation_outcome_clean",
            row.get("specific_trait", np.nan),
        )

        rows.append(f"""
        <tr>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('pgs_id', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('ppm_id', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('pss_id', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(cohort_display_value(row))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(outcome)}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(" · ".join(discrimination_parts) if discrimination_parts else None)}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(odds)}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(hazard)}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(beta_text)}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(r2_text)}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(other_metrics_text)}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(fmt_int(row.get('evaluation_n', np.nan)))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(row.get('broad_ancestry_category', np.nan))}</td>
          <td>{model_table_value(pub)}</td>
        </tr>
        """)

    return "\n".join(rows)
